why: The change is needed and the old text was wrong (lines 515 to 523 are syncStore's session code, the column is state, and state <> 'synced' would list every store with a blocked row on every tick), and copying claim()'s due condition is the right idea. But the new condition compares with the database's now() instead of the run's clock, misses the PDF attachments the sync does on later ticks, the connection changes, and the mode/company filter, and leaves Work's time columns and three registry caps for the executor to guess: as written it breaks four existing int-test assertions. With the exact statement below it is safe for a cheap model with review.

problems.what: Old text wrong: lines 515 to 523 are syncStore() (getTripletexConnection, sweep, claim), not a table; the sync table is commerce.tripletex_sync with a state column; state <> 'synced' includes blocked, drifted and skipped rows, which stay for ever, so every store with one would be listed every tick. The editor's correction is right.

The due test uses the database's now(); claim() compares with the run's own clock (options.now). Existing cases that move the clock (sync(tx, storeId, later(2)) after a failure) would find the store not listed and fail.

PDF attachment is work the sync does on a later tick without any new document or due row: a shop document is booked, its PDF is made minutes later, and attachable() picks it up on the next run. The condition does not cover it, so every shop PDF waits up to an hour and the existing assertions attached: 1 fail.

The due exists lacks claim()'s mode/company_id (Fiken: company_slug) filter. Sync rows are kept after a disconnect; a pending or failed row of an earlier company is never claimed, so the store would be listed on every tick for ever.
problems.evidence: src/server/tripletex-sync.ts:126; fiken-sync.ts:114; schema.ts:7929 ('Kept when a store disconnects')

problems.what: An auth_failed store is in the list (for its daily alert), and the auth failure releases its rows with next_attempt_at null, so they are due: the store would be listed every tick while the token is refused, for nothing (syncStore returns at once).

Connection changes (Start, resume, settings such as sources or attachPdf, start day moved back, reconnect after auth_failed, a new company) create work without a new document; looked_at was written hourly while auth_failed, so documents issued then wait up to an hour after the reconnect. The writers already set updated_at, so c.updated_at > c.looked_at covers them for free.

'<its issue time column>' leaves the Work columns to the executor. work_invoices has no issued_at; issued_on can be back-dated; sent_at is set to now() at issue (and imported invoices are excluded by the sweep). work_credit_notes has created_at only.

looked_at = now() written after the turn misses a document issued during the turn (after sweep(), before the update) for an hour. It must be the time taken before the sweep (now() returned by the list statement), written only when syncStore() did not throw.

exists on invoices/credit_notes by issued_at alone has no index (only (store_id, issued_on)): every tick reads every invoice of each connected shop. Bound it with issued_on >= the store day of looked_at minus 1.

Registry: tripletex, fiken and ledger caps (40 s) and orders match the code. autoArchive, autopilotBudgets and recurring have no store limit; 'the number of stores it can do in its budgetMs' cannot be read from code (a guess), and 'adding order by' edits files the change list does not name.

Tests miss the cases that tell a wrong condition apart: a failed row not yet due (not listed) then due by the run's clock (listed), a row of another company (not listed), auth_failed with due rows (not listed), a settings change (listed), a Work invoice and a shop invoice (listed), and 'listed' needs an observable (looked_at moving).

syncDueTripletex() (line 645). (1) Move `const now = (options.now ?? (() => new Date()))();` (line 660) to the top of the function, before the try, and let nowIso = now.toISOString(); the list must use the run's clock exactly as claim() does (lines 127 and 128 compare with ${now.toISOString()}::timestamptz, never with now()), or the existing cases that pass later(2) (tripletex-sync.int.test.ts line 147, fiken.int.test.ts line 291) stop finding their retry. (2) Replace the list statement (lines 651 to 653) with this one, adding listed_at: col.timestamp to its zod object:
select c.store_id, s.time_zone, now() as listed_at
  from commerce.tripletex_connections c join commerce.stores s on s.id = c.store_id
 where c.state in ('on', 'auth_failed') and s.status = 'active'
   and (c.looked_at is null
     or c.looked_at < ${nowIso}::timestamptz - interval '1 hour'
     or (c.state = 'on' and (
          c.updated_at > c.looked_at
       or exists (select 1 from commerce.invoices i where i.store_id = c.store_id and i.issued_on >= (c.looked_at at time zone s.time_zone)::date - 1 and i.issued_at > c.looked_at)
       or exists (select 1 from commerce.credit_notes n where n.store_id = c.store_id and n.issued_on >= (c.looked_at at time zone s.time_zone)::date - 1 and n.issued_at > c.looked_at)
       or exists (select 1 from commerce.work_invoices w where w.store_id = c.store_id and w.status <> 'draft' and not w.imported and w.sent_at > c.looked_at)
       or exists (select 1 from commerce.work_credit_notes wc where wc.store_id = c.store_id and wc.created_at > c.looked_at)
       or exists (select 1 from commerce.tripletex_sync y
                   where y.store_id = c.store_id and y.mode = c.mode and y.company_id = c.company_id and y.kind <> 'customer'
                     and ((y.state in ('pending', 'failed') and coalesce(y.next_attempt_at, '-infinity') <= ${nowIso}::timestamptz)
                       or (y.state = 'sending' and y.claimed_until < ${nowIso}::timestamptz)))
       or (coalesce((c.settings ->> 'attachPdf')::boolean, true) and exists (
            select 1 from commerce.tripletex_sync y
              left join commerce.invoices si on y.kind = 'shop_invoice' and si.store_id = y.store_id and si.id::text = y.local_id
              left join commerce.credit_notes sc on y.kind = 'shop_credit_note' and sc.store_id = y.store_id and sc.id::text = y.local_id
             where y.store_id = c.store_id and y.mode = c.mode and y.company_id = c.company_id
               and y.kind in ('shop_invoice', 'shop_credit_note') and y.state = 'synced' and y.attached_at is null and y.their_id is not null
               and y.attach_tries < ${ATTACH_TRIES} and y.synced_at > ${nowIso}::timestamptz - make_interval(days => ${ATTACH_DAYS})
               and coalesce(si.pdf_path, sc.pdf_path) is not null and coalesce(si.anonymised_at, sc.anonymised_at) is null))
     )))
 order by c.last_ok_at nulls first
Why each part, so none is dropped: the due exists is claim()'s own condition (lines 125 to 128) including its mode and company filter (rows of an earlier company are kept after a disconnect and would otherwise list the store every tick for ever); the attach exists is attachable()'s condition (line 581) without its limit, because a shop document's PDF is made a few minutes after it is booked and the existing case at tripletex-sync.int.test.ts line 399 attaches it on the next run; c.updated_at catches Start, resume, a settings or start-day change and a reconnect (each writer in src/server/tripletex.ts sets updated_at; the sync's own writes do not); the four document exists are what sweep() inserts from (shop invoices and credit notes by issued_at, bounded by issued_on, the store day, so the (store_id, issued_on) index is used; a Work invoice by sent_at, which commerce.issue_work_invoice sets to now() while issued_on may be back-dated; a Work credit note by created_at); an auth_failed store is listed only hourly, for its daily alert. ATTACH_TRIES and ATTACH_DAYS are the constants at lines 576 to 578; define them above syncDueTripletex() if they are declared below it. (3) In the loop, inside the try right after `await syncStore(store.id, options, run, deadline);` (line 664) and only when it did not throw: `await db().execute(sql\`update commerce.tripletex_connections set looked_at = ${store.listedAt}::timestamptz where store_id = ${store.id}::uuid\`)` where listedAt is the row's listed_at (carry it in the mapped store objects). It is the database's time before this run's sweep, so a document issued during the turn is still newer than looked_at; never write now() there. A store the loop did not reach (the deadline) keeps its looked_at. Keep `order by c.last_ok_at nulls first`, the storeIds filter, the 40 s budget, syncStore() and claim() unchanged; no session is opened for a store with nothing to send. (4) The same in src/server/fiken-sync.ts syncDueFiken() (line 520; now at line 535; list at lines 526 to 528; syncStore call at line 539): commerce.fiken_connections and commerce.fiken_sync, and in both exists on fiken_sync `y.company_slug = c.company_slug` in place of `y.mode = c.mode and y.company_id = c.company_id` (claim() lines 113 to 116, attachable() line 414, its ATTACH_TRIES and ATTACH_DAYS); everything else word for word. Read docs/tripletex.md and docs/fiken.md first: if either promises a delay shorter than an hour for something this condition does not list, stop.

The registry is DISPATCHER_JOBS in this file (step 1.10 moved it here, step 3.3 made each entry `{ every, why, work, budgetMs, run }`); the route is not changed, and no other file is changed for this part. Set `work` exactly to: ledger `{ perStore: { cap: 40, order: "checked_at nulls first, id (seconds a run)" } }` (the order step 3.22 gave runLedgerPosting()); tripletex and fiken `{ perStore: { cap: 40, order: "last_ok_at nulls first (seconds a run)" } }` (BUDGET_MS 40_000 in each file); autoArchive `{ perStore: { cap: Infinity, order: "unordered: every active store with auto_archive_days, 200 orders each (AUTO_ARCHIVE_BATCH)" } }` (src/server/order-archive.ts line 116: no store limit, no order by); autopilotBudgets `{ perStore: { cap: Infinity, order: "unordered: every active store with an AI budget, not paused" } }` (src/server/autopilot-settings.ts line 98); recurring `{ perStore: { cap: Infinity, order: "id: stores with Work and an active repeating invoice, 500 templates each (MAX_TEMPLATES_PER_STORE)" } }` (src/server/work-recurring.ts line 694). Do not add an order by or a limit to those three functions. Confirm autoArchive, autopilotBudgets and recurring have every 3600 (step 3.3 set them); set it if not. If step 3.3's type or scan refuses Infinity as a cap, stop and report.

Leave every existing case and assertion as it is: they must pass unchanged (a failure there means the condition is wrong; stop). Add one describe block 'skipping a store with nothing new' to src/server/tripletex-sync.int.test.ts; "listed" is read as looked_at moving: lookedAt(storeId) selects looked_at from commerce.tripletex_connections. Cases, each on a store connected and synced once with sync(): (a) set looked_at = now() - interval '1 minute'; sync() leaves looked_at unchanged and, measured with countStatements() from '@/db/statement-count', sends exactly 1 statement; (b) then issue a Work invoice (issued(actor, clientId)): the next sync() books it (sent: 1) and moves looked_at; (c) a shop invoice (fx.paidOrder as in the 'sending the shop's invoices' block) is booked on the next sync() the same way; (d) with a row made failed by tx.failNext('POST', /^\/ledger\/voucher$/, 503) and looked_at set a minute back: sync() leaves looked_at unchanged, sync(tx, storeId, later(2)) books it; (e) a pending row of another company (insert into commerce.tripletex_sync a work_invoice row with company_id + 1 and state 'pending') with looked_at a minute back: sync() leaves looked_at unchanged; (f) with looked_at a minute back, update commerce.tripletex_connections set updated_at = now() (what every owner-side writer does): the next sync() moves looked_at; (g) the connection set to auth_failed with a pending due row and looked_at a minute back: not listed; with looked_at two hours back: listed; (h) with nothing new and looked_at two hours back: listed. The same cases in src/server/fiken.int.test.ts with fiken_connections, fiken_sync and company_slug || '-old' for (e).

A connected store with nothing new costing statements on every tick; a store whose only rows are a retry not yet due, rows of an earlier company, or an auth_failed store's released rows being listed every tick; and a new Work or shop document, a retry coming due by the run's clock, a PDF made after booking or a connection change waiting for the hourly look.

docs/tripletex.md and docs/fiken.md: an idle store is looked at hourly; a new document, a retry coming due, a PDF made after its document was booked and a change to the connection are taken on the next five-minute tick.

Do not open a Tripletex or Fiken session for a store with nothing to send, and do not change the 40-second budget, the storeIds filter, syncStore(), claim() or attachable(); do not change any existing assertion in tripletex-sync.int.test.ts or fiken.int.test.ts.
